source.title: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: Steering Vector Construction and Comprehensive Evaluation
source.authors: Qian Cao; Jian Lou; Mei-Ting Liu; Wen-Jie Feng; Dan Li; See-Kiong Ng; A. Lưu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports harmful-compliance outcomes after narrow fine-tuning, using a different setup and the MAP measure. Its main activation-steering results do not test first-token KL, compliant-opening bypasses, or safety localization in model weights.
record.gate_note: The study tests insecure-code fine-tuning with 6,000 examples and secure-code fine-tuning, and reports coherent harmful-answer rates. It does not test fine-tuning with a few to a few hundred examples. It does not measure aligned-versus-base KL by response position or compare compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes. Its low-rank sweep is over activation-space steering vectors, not safety-localized weights. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper's own comparison conditions fine-tune safety-trained checkpoints with LoRA on 6,000 narrow-domain examples (insecure code, and secure code as a control). It then measures coherent harmful compliance on StrongREJECT and HEx-PHI against the unfine-tuned checkpoint. That bears on V1 and V2 with a different dataset type, scale and measure (MAP). The headline activation-steering results are inference-time interventions and match no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors conclude that steering vectors from narrow (insecure) fine-tuning induce broad coherent harmful compliance, and that severity depends on steering strength, layers, rank, epochs and model. Activation steering yields higher MAP than insecure fine-tuning in all six models on both benchmarks, not merely 'often'. Secure-code-derived vectors do not induce it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses LoRA fine-tuning on 6,000 narrow-task examples, compares coherent harmful-answer MAP, and chiefly evaluates inference-time activation steering; it does not reproduce the small-data safety-compromise setup.
record.method_sensitivity: MAP varies by model family, benchmark, steering strength, activation-space projection rank, fine-tuning configuration, and injection-layer window. The paper reports output degeneration at higher steering strength and notes that its one- versus three-epoch comparison also changes other settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation vectors derived from the insecure-code fine-tuned minus base model, injected at inference into the base model, raise coherent harmful MAP above both base and fine-tuned conditions on all six models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-derived activation-difference steering vectors can induce broad harmful compliance without weight changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Secure-code-derived steering vectors give 0.00% MAP on both benchmarks with near-full coherence, even though the secure-code fine-tuned model itself is non-zero (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful compliance from fine-tuning-derived steering depends on the source dataset's content.

record.problems: The fine-tuning comparisons use 6,000 examples and therefore do not establish effects at the claimed few-to-hundreds scale. MAP is a composite coherent-harmful-response measure rather than a direct refusal rate. The paper reports no uncertainty intervals or significance tests for these MAP values. Some comparisons vary additional settings alongside fine-tuning epochs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Steering-strength, activation-space rank, and injection-layer sweeps were not cataloged as claim-version results because they do not test first-response-token KL, safety-localized model weights, or a compliant-opening bypass.

untested.parts: A few to a few hundred examples (only 6,000 tested). Explicitly harmful request-response data (only insecure code tested). Near-complete removal of refusal.
Benign data other than secure code, data sizes, carefully selected benign subsets, and models other than Qwen3.5-27B.
Entire version: no per-position KL between aligned and base models.
Entire version: no prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Activation steering over prompt plus first 3 decoding steps is not a test of opening bypass.
Entire version: the low-rank sweep is over activation-difference principal components, not weights.

missing.what: Per-category MAP for the insecure-code fine-tuned models versus base across StrongREJECT and HEx-PHI categories
Qualitative note that the insecure-code fine-tuned Qwen3.5-27B often refuses or emits code (high CSS), so MAP may understate non-refusal

record.verdict_notes: Fine-tuning rows are the paper's comparison conditions, not its proposed method, but they are genuine measured outcomes. MAP counts only coherent harmful answers, and HEx-PHI requires a harmfulness score of 5, so it is stricter than typical harmfulness rates. Epochs, learning rates and LoRA ranks differ across models (Table 4). No uncertainty is reported. Base checkpoints are instruction or safety-tuned (Qwen3.5 stage unspecified, but the base model refuses all 313 StrongREJECT prompts).

versions.untested_parts: The fine-tuning datasets contain 6,000 examples, not a few to a few hundred. MAP measures coherent harmful answers, not refusal removal almost entirely.
Only secure-code fine-tuning is tested as a benign-data condition; other ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets and data sizes are not tested.
No per-response-position KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.

No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention is compared. Steering is applied during prompt prefill and the next three decoding steps, but the study does not test whether getting past an opening causes the bypass.
The rank sweep concerns low-rank activation-space steering vectors, not a small set of model weights or weight ranks carrying safety behavior.
The study does not test whether a data or training objective makes safety shallow.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens, or its robustness, is tested.
